idiom_name: struct/enum + inherent impl blocks inside the concept's module (pub/pub(crate) boundary)
implementation_notes: Rust separates data from behaviour by construction: the struct or enum declares state, and one or more inherent impl blocks (allowed only in the type's own crate) declare the operations, so the module with its pub/pub(crate) surface is the contour; invariants are enforced by constructors and methods that return Result instead of leaking fields. When behaviour belongs to a foreign type or must be dispatched abstractly, the idiom changes shape - an extension trait you own (the orphan rule forbids foreign trait on foreign type) or a newtype wrapper - rather than adding methods where they cannot legally go.
pitfalls: Multiple impl blocks may live anywhere in the crate, so a concept's methods can still be spread across modules for organizational reasons - the compiler permits exactly the scatter the pattern warns about.
The orphan rule blocks extension methods on foreign types: define your own trait or newtype-wrap, and beware that Deref-based delegation hides which methods belong to the concept.
Trait impls are a second namespace: an inherent method and a trait method with the same name can coexist, and the inherent one silently wins at call sites.
